title: Body effect: threshold shift and gmb

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
The body of a MOSFET is a fourth terminal that acts as a **back gate**. Raising the source above the body (\(V_{SB} > 0\) for NMOS) widens the depletion region under the channel. The extra bulk charge must be supported before inversion, so the threshold rises. The reader derives the size of the shift from the MOS threshold expression. It grows as a square root of \(-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}\), scaled by the body-effect coefficient \(\gamma\).

When the source-body voltage carries a signal, the back gate also modulates the current. The **body transconductance** \(g_{mb}\) is the slope of \(I_D\) with respect to \(V_{BS}\). By the chain rule through \(V_T\) it is a fraction \(\eta\) of \(g_m\), typically 0.1 to 0.3. In the four-terminal model \(g_{mb}v_{bs}\) sits in parallel with \(g_mv_{gs}\) from drain to source. The effect disappears only when source and body are tied together, which a PMOS in its own well can do.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ V_T = V_{T0} + \gamma\left(\sqrt{-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}} - \sqrt{-2\varphi_p}\right), \qquad \gamma = \frac{\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_{si}N_A}}{C_{ox}} \]
\[ g_{mb} = \eta g_m, \qquad \eta = \frac{\gamma}{2\sqrt{-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}}}, \qquad i_d = g_mv_{gs} + g_{mb}v_{bs} + \frac{v_{ds}}{r_o} \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: With \(\gamma = 0.6\ \mathrm{V^{1/2}}\), \(-2\varphi_p = 0.9\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{SB} = 2.7\ \mathrm{V}\), the threshold rises by \(0.6(\sqrt{3.6} - \sqrt{0.9}) = 0.6(1.897 - 0.949) = 0.57\ \mathrm{V}\). At that bias \(\eta = 0.6/(2\cdot1.897) = 0.16\), so a device with \(g_m = 3\ \mathrm{mS}\) has \(g_{mb} \approx 0.47\ \mathrm{mS}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Writing \(\gamma\sqrt{V_{SB}}\) and forgetting the \(-2\varphi_p\) terms.
- Assuming a grounded body means no body effect; a source above ground still has \(V_{SB} > 0\).
- Getting the sign of \(g_{mb}v_{bs}\) wrong; raising the body increases current. (Reader Eq. 10.8 carries a sign slip on the \(V_{SB}\) term; Eq. 10.9 is correct.)

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: The body effect lowers source-follower gain and output resistance, and it shifts bias in stacked circuits such as cascodes.
